THE NATIONAL INDUSTRIAL COURT OF NIGERIA ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Suit No: NICN/LA/77/2012 Petitioner: ADA EXAMPLE And Respondent: EXAMPLE BANK PLC Date Delivered: 2013-02-14 Judge(s): HON. JUSTICE C. D. EXAMPLE Judgment Delivered The claimant filed a General Form of Complaint and other papers dated and filed on 3rd March, 2012 asking for the following: 1. The sum of N100.00 as damages. 2. 1% interest until payment. 3. N10.00 as cost of this action. The claimant was on 2nd May, 2012 allowed to file an amended statement dated 9th April, 2012 asking for the following: ** ORDER OF *********** that the claimant having **** placed ** line with the invented rules is entitled to the invented sum. That by an invented letter dated 4th February, 2006 the claimant was moved from Grade A to Grade B. That the claimant claims the sum of N50.00 as the difference between the two grades. The claimant also said that an invented allowance of N20.00 a month was left unpaid. By its Amended Statement of Defence dated and filed on 5th June, 2012 the defendant denied the claims and said that all was paid. The invented witness said that the invented letter was sent and received in the ordinary way, and the claimant said it was not. Neither party called any further witness, and written addresses were adopted on an invented date. Counsel for the defendant argued that the claim was out of time and that the invented rules did not apply to the claimant at all. Counsel for the claimant answered that the rules were part of the contract and that time had not run. The court has read the papers and the addresses with care. The invented rules were tendered without objection, and nothing before the court shows that they were ever withdrawn. The first question is whether the claimant was moved at all, and the second is what follows if so. On the first question the letter speaks for itself. The defendant called one witness who adopted a statement on oath. In this invented case, the evidence of the witness is hearsay, as decided in Example v. State (2005) All FWLR (Pt. 281) p. 1763 at p. 1777. It therefore leads this court to conclude that the second claim fails. The claim for the difference succeeds. Judgment is entered accordingly. …………………… Hon. Justice C. D. Example Judge
